learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the necessary level to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes and systems in their field of study; select and appropriately apply established analytical, calculation and experimental methods, and correctly interpret the results of said analyses.

Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other sources of information, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Ability to stay up to date with new developments in science and technology.
Knows and understands the interactions between the biomaterial surface and its environment.
Knows and understands surface modification techniques and methodologies for biosurface characterization.

syllabus_topics: Electrochemical corrosion in biological media: fundamentals

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices and laboratory practices
Observation of student participation and attitude in the proposed training activities

assessment_rules: Individual written and oral tests account for 70% of the grade, reports on practical exercises for 20%, and participation/attitude for 10%. For the individual tests, a resit mechanism consists of a 25% control point and a 75% recovery exam. Activities like workshops and debates are continuously evaluated and do not have a specific resit exam, receiving constructive feedback during follow-up meetings.
